name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+12 partisan baseline)
Tokuda's overwhelming financial advantage ($570k on hand vs. $16k)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no serious outside spending against her
model.rationale: Hawaii's second district leans heavily Democratic, incumbent Jill Tokuda is running again, and she has out-raised Brenton Awa by roughly seven to one with a huge cash-on-hand edge. Prediction markets price her near-certain to win, and no polling or expert ratings suggest a competitive race, so the fundamentals-based expectation of a low-twenties Democratic margin stands.
model.watch: Any late surge in Awa's fundraising or outside Republican spending, or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race, would be the main signal that this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's second congressional district covers rural and outer-island areas and leans strongly Democratic, giving Democrats a baseline edge of roughly twelve points before incumbency and the political environment are added. Jill Tokuda, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election after first winning the seat in 2022.

Her Republican challenger, Brenton Awa, has raised about $123,000 and holds roughly $16,000 on hand, while Tokuda has raised over $820,000 with about $570,000 available and modest outside support behind her. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, but prediction markets put Tokuda's chances around 96 percent. The combination of the district's lean, incumbency, and the money gap points to a comfortable Democratic win with a margin in the low twenties.
